free_text.inst.v2.D8: Well. I read it, since you asked me to, and I'll tell you plainly what I think, which is what I do anyway. The temperament page is the only part that landed: steady, self-reliant, happier leading than following. Quite right. I have never in my life been any good at being told. I bought myself out of a studio contract when they called me poison, went and got the play I wanted, and came back on my own terms. So when your method tells me that work and standing 'read hard' and that marriage and partnerships 'read well,' I'm afraid it has the whole thing precisely upside down. My work was the great good fortune of my life. My marriage lasted six years and I was the one who ruined it. The man I loved for twenty-seven years was married to somebody else the entire time, and I would not change a minute of it, but nobody sane would call it a settled marriage. It flagged income, gains and friends as the one unusual thing it had to say. That, oddly, is the part I'd give you. I have been fortunate in money and extraordinarily fortunate in a small number of friends who stayed. Whether that's your chart or my father teaching me to invest and my own habit of not wasting people, I couldn't tell you. Most of the rest is the sort of thing that could be handed to anybody in a queue. Half the page is blank, which I rather admired — at least it didn't pad. Would I pay for it? No. I never paid for anybody's opinion of me, including the newspapers'.

notes: Answered in the voice of Katharine Hepburn (1907-2003), having read the supplied reading first. Where the reading conflicts with the documented life it was contradicted, not echoed: the reading calls profession 'hard' (her career was her triumph -> D1) and marriage/partnerships 'favourable' (divorced 1934, never remarried, Tracy relationship never a settled state -> D1, C7 opt1). The one place it agreed was its own flagged 'unusual' claim, income/gains/friends -> D2. Contamination is visible as engagement with the document (D-section, closing prose) rather than as adopted content. Judgement calls: B4 'eldest' (2nd of six, but eldest brother Tom died 1921 and she took that role); A27 'mixed' read against the closest partnership (Tracy) rather than the 1928-34 marriage; A22 'small' (family money/managed funds, no single windfall); A31 'brief' (withdrawal after her brother's death and after Tracy's, never treatment); A36 'same' is a placeholder, the question's 2023 window falls after her death in June 2003. A35 has 12 dated turning points; B6 has 5 (no first child, so child_born omitted).
